children.name: Pelliciera benthamii  Cornejo
children.description: Pelliciera benthamii Cornejo — a neotropical mangrove tree recently elevated from varietal to species rank (Cornejo & Bonifaz, 2020) based on genetic, morphological, and ecological evidence. Distinguished from P. rhizophorae by pink to crimson-red floral bracts (vs white/cream), smaller stature resembling a dwarf version, and dentate leaf margins. Native to the Caribbean coast from Panama to northern Colombia, occupying the understory of Rhizophora-dominated mangroves in low-salinity zones. Flowers are large, showy, pentamerous, visited by hummingbirds and potentially bats; fruits are viviparous propagules.

children.name: Pelliciera rhizophoreae Triana & Planch.
children.description: Pelliciera rhizophoreae Triana & Planch. — a taxonomic variant spelling of P. rhizophorae, the tea mangrove, a neotropical mangrove tree found along the Pacific coast from the Gulf of Nicoya (Costa Rica) to the Esmeraldas River (Ecuador), with small stands in Nicaragua, Panama, and Colombia on the Caribbean side. Grows up to 20 m tall with large, showy, pentamerous flowers with white to cream floral bracts, pollinated by bats (Glossophaga soricina) and hummingbirds. Produces viviparous propagules. Listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List; threatened by coastal development, logging, and sea-level rise. Fossil records date to the Eocene, making it one of the oldest known mangrove lineages.

children.name: Tetramerista glabra Miq.
children.description: Tetramerista glabra Miq. — an evergreen mid-canopy tree reaching up to 37 m tall with a fluted base, small buttresses, and leathery, glabrous leaves with marginal pit-glands. Native to western Malesia (Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo), where it grows in freshwater and peat swamp forests, mangroves, and mixed dipterocarp forests up to 200 m altitude. Flowers tetramerous, greenish-yellow to golden, 13–25 mm across, borne in axillary panicles. Fruit a round berry 15–30 mm wide, green to purple, with edible sour pulp; seeds oblong, 10–15 mm. Wood is light yellow-brown with pink tinges, used for fencing, planks, posts, and firewood. Also known locally as Entuyut or Punah.

children.name: Pentamerista neotropica Maguire
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to (Guainía) to Venezuela (Amazonas) and NW. Brazil. It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.
